subject: Comp band anchoring methodology and offer velocity guidance
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Comp band anchoring methodology and offer velocity guidance

Team — attaching Mercer's regional benchmarking and the current anchor model (v3). Key asks: can we converge on a single anchoring approach for senior ICs (L4-L6) that is geo-relative (US base, EU adjustors) and a separate localized approach for manager tiers?

Context: recruiting is flagging longer offer cycles in EMEA and candidates are seeing inconsistent anchors between hiring managers. I think standardizing an anchor curve + a simple multiplier by region will speed approvals and reduce negotiation variance.

Please review the two things in the attachment: 1) the proposed "anchor curve" (compband_anchor_model_v3.xlsx) and 2) Mercer benchmarking PDF — page 18 has median and 75th percentiles by market.

Concrete asks:
- Laura: can you confirm operational constraints for applying a single anchor curve across hiring flows? (approvals, payroll limits)
- Neha: recommend guardrails for offer velocity exceptions (what warrants an escalation to Talent Ops + Finance)
- Marissa: can the CS/Platform managers get a separate localized anchor or do we keep uniformity?
- Karthik: headcount approvals impact — any timing / budget notes to watch.

I propose we meet Tuesday at 10am PT to lock rules and a one-page playbook for recruiters.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Talent Strategy | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: mercer_compband_us_eu_2027Q1.pdf, compband_anchor_model_v3.xlsx

Cc: Ava Recruiting <ava@hiringpartner.io>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Comp band anchoring methodology and offer velocity guidance

Jonas — thanks for the packet. We've added a short appendix that highlights the 90/75/50 percentile spreads for each geography and modeled a simple multiplier ladder that preserves internal parity while reflecting local market pressure. See attached PDF (mercer_compband_us_eu_2027Q1.pdf).

A few quick notes from our side:
- For senior ICs, our recommended approach is a US-anchor + geo multiplier (France: -12%, Germany: -8%, UK: -5%) rather than re-anchoring per market; this keeps internal equity for distributed teams.
- Managers and above: re-anchor per-market with narrow bands to reflect localized hiring comp patterns.
- Offer velocity: we recommend a two-tier exception path — recruiter + hiring manager can approve up to 5% above anchor; anything above that requires Talent Ops + Finance sign-off.

Happy to run a short calibration call with Talent Ops and Hiring Managers.

Best,
Sonia Patel
Engagement Lead, Mercer Talent Solutions
talent@mercer.com

Agree with Mercer on the two-path approach. Operational notes from Payroll / Benefits:
- We can support a US-anchor + multiplier approach for base offers but the offer letter system needs the explicit local currency fields filled; recruiters must mark the anchor and multiplier used for audit logs.
- Exceptions that trigger Finance must land before the payroll cutoff for the hire month. If an exception is approved after payroll cutoff, compensation will be processed as an adjustment after hire (we should avoid this).

I'll coordinate a short runbook for recruiters to include in the ATS offer flow (one-pager). Draft due EOD Wednesday.

- Laura

Thanks — quick principles for offer velocity exceptions:
1) Market urgency: evidence (competing offer, counter) required (forwarded email from recruiter is fine).
2) Candidate performance: must document interview matrix score and hiring manager justification.
3) Business impact: role criticality (revenue/ops risk) documented in the request.

Approval routing (recommended):
- <=5% above anchor: recruiter + hiring manager sign-off (no Finance)
- 5–12%: Talent Ops review (Laura) + hiring manager
- >12% or above the 90th market percentile: requires Finance and CEO People Office sign-off (Jonas)

I'll prepare a template form for exceptions and an automated review tag in the ATS to track SLA.

— Neha

Quick note from people managers: for Platform and CS managers, there's more local variation in Prague and Lisbon — I'd prefer localized anchors for those teams. However, I support keeping ICs on the US-anchor + multiplier to preserve cross-region parity.

If we allow localized anchors for managers we should:
- cap local anchoring to +/-6% of the US-anchor unless a documented business case exists;
- require a Director-level approval for local anchor deviations.

I can pilot this with two hires in EMEA next month and report back.
